title: When the Spire Burns
premise: In the city of Vellamark, magic was outlawed a generation ago after the Spire—the bridge between the human realm and the dragon-realm of Ashkarat—was burned by royal decree. Paloma Sterling, a temple scribe bound by debt and hiding a small gift for charm-crafting, is exposed during the crown's great hunt and forced to flee with a stolen relic: the Ember Codex, which holds the terms of the original covenant between realms. Hunted by Inquisitor Dain Corvane—a man whose own suppressed gift makes him both her greatest threat and her reluctant mirror—Paloma discovers the covenant was broken not by dragons but by the first king's greed, and that the dying dragon-fire is what keeps the city's memory intact. To reforge the covenant she must climb the ruined Spire and offer something irreplaceable: her memories of everyone she has ever loved. The novel ends with Paloma ascending the burning Spire, sacrificing her past to reignite the flame, while Corvane chooses to preserve her story in writing so that who she was is never fully lost.
about_author: Ada Oyelaran is a former archivist who spent years cataloguing colonial-era manuscripts before turning to fiction full-time. She writes fantasy about debt, memory, and the institutions people survive inside, and lives between Lagos and Lisbon.

chapters.title: Small Charms
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. We meet her selling minor charms in Vellamark's night market, counting coins against her crushing temple debt, and concealing the warmth in her fingertips that marks her gift. A child pays with a button; Paloma charms it anyway. Emotional beat: weary tenderness, the quiet cost of hiding.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Criers announce the crown's hunt for the gifted; temple wards begin testing scribes. Paloma passes by numbing her hands in ice water, but a fellow scribe, Ivet, fails and is dragged away screaming her name. Emotional beat: fear sharpened into survivor's guilt.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Keeps
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Searching the temple archive for leverage over her debt, Paloma finds references to the Ember Codex and the true terms of the old covenant. She realizes the official history of the Spire's burning is a forgery. Emotional beat: the vertigo of discovering your whole world rests on a lie.

chapters.title: Ash on the Wind
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Introduced as the Inquisitor leading the hunt, suppressing his own gift with iron cuffs. He interrogates Ivet and recognizes in her terror his younger self. He is ordered to sweep the temple archives next. Emotional beat: duty curdling into dread.

chapters.title: Theft
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. With hours before Corvane arrives, Paloma steals the Ember Codex from the sealed reliquary, triggering an alarm that burns her name into the hunt rolls. Her mentor, Mother Sefu, covers her escape at terrible cost. Emotional beat: the point of no return, chosen rather than stumbled into.

chapters.title: The Low Roads
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Fleeing through the flooded undercity, Paloma bargains passage with Tamsin, a smuggler who owes the temple nothing and trusts no one. First glimpse of the guttering dragon-fire visible from below like a dying star. Emotional beat: grudging alliance, loneliness interrupted.

chapters.title: Iron and Ink
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Corvane finds Mother Sefu alive but broken; she gives him a false trail and one true sentence: 'The covenant was ours to break.' His superiors order him to burn the archive. He copies one page first. Emotional beat: the first hairline crack in his loyalty.

chapters.title: The Ember Codex
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Reading the Codex by candlelight, Paloma learns the covenant required mutual offering—human memory for dragon-fire—and that the first king took the fire and gave nothing. The realms are dying of the imbalance. Emotional beat: awe and fury braided together.

chapters.title: A Market of the Marked
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Tamsin leads Paloma to a hidden enclave of the hunted gifted, where charms are survival tools, not crimes. Paloma is asked to prove herself and heals a dying woman's pain at real physical cost. Emotional beat: belonging offered, and its price made visible.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Ordered to raid the enclave, Corvane goes—and lets eleven people escape through a door he 'fails' to guard. But his lieutenant sees. Now Corvane is hunted too. Emotional beat: the moment complicity becomes betrayal.

chapters.title: Two Fugitives
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Corvane catches up to Paloma intending arrest; instead they are ambushed by crown wardens gone rogue, and forced to fight side by side. Each recognizes the other's suppressed gift. Uneasy truce struck over a campfire. Emotional beat: enemies discovering a shared wound.

chapters.title: What Memory Is For
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The Codex reveals the reforging price: a willing human must carry their dearest memories up the Spire and give them to the flame. Paloma inventories what she would lose—her mother's voice, Ivet's laugh. Emotional beat: grief rehearsed in advance.

chapters.title: The Dragon's Shadow
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. At the Spire's base, the last dragon, Vessharran, ancient and half-blind, tests them. It shows Corvane the truth of the first king's theft through shared memory. Corvane removes his iron cuffs and does not die. Emotional beat: liberation that feels like falling.

chapters.title: The City Turns Out
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Word spreads that the Spire will be climbed; the crown declares martial law. Tamsin organizes the enclave and sympathetic smugglers to hold the streets—not for glory, but to buy the climbers time. Emotional beat: ordinary courage massing into defiance.

chapters.title: Mother Sefu's Confession
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Dying, Mother Sefu admits she helped forge the false history decades ago to protect the temple's position, and begs Paloma's forgiveness. Paloma cannot give it yet. Emotional beat: forgiveness withheld honestly, love persisting anyway.

chapters.title: The Climb Begins
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Under cover of Tamsin's street riots, Paloma and Corvane enter the Spire's root and begin the ascent through collapsing galleries where burned covenant-magic still smolders. The fire tests each with visions of their worst choices. Emotional beat: ascent as judgment.

chapters.title: Corvane's Choice
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The Spire offers Corvane restoration—his gift returned, his guilt erased—if he abandons Paloma. He refuses, naming his guilt aloud and carrying it upward. Warden forces breach the Spire behind them. Emotional beat: redemption earned by refusing the easy version.

chapters.title: The Last Offer
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. At the summit, the flame demands its price. Paloma begins surrendering her memories—her mother, Ivet, the market, her own name—while below, Tamsin's people hold the gates and fall one by one. Emotional beat: sacrifice rendered intimate, not heroic.

chapters.title: When the Spire Burns
chapters.summary: Climax, alternating POVs. The Spire ignites anew as the covenant reforges; dragon-fire floods the realm and the city's stolen memories return to it like rain. Corvane, half-burned, holds the dying Paloma and refuses to let the flame take everything. Emotional beat: devastation and dawn in the same breath.

chapters.title: The Written Woman
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Paloma survives, hollowed—her past gone—but Corvane has spent the climb writing down every memory she spoke aloud. He reads her back to herself, page by page. Some things return; some only exist now in ink. Emotional beat: love as authorship, identity as collaborative act.

chapters.title: A New Covenant
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Months later: the city reckons with its forged history, the temple's power broken, dragons and humans negotiating openly. Tamsin, scarred and pragmatic, declines every honor offered. Emotional beat: the unglamorous work of rebuilding, chosen freely.

chapters.title: Small Charms, Again
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Paloma returns to the night market, debt-free, selling small charms openly—some hers, some gifts from Vessharran. A child pays with a button. She no longer remembers why the gesture matters so much, only that it does. Emotional beat: quiet, hard-won peace; memory outlived by meaning.
